title: Vesper and the Letters
premise: Marguerite Okafor, a pastry chef three missed payments from losing her café, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of Vesper Adeyemi—a festival planner and estranged heir to the family whose reunion she's dreading—in exchange for a catering contract that could save everything. What begins as a transactional lie deepens over shared desserts and late-night letters Vesper writes but never sends, until Marguerite discovers the contract was contingent on her helping Vesper secure an inheritance built on displacing her own neighborhood. At the festival's climax, Marguerite must choose between signing the deal that saves her café and exposing the corruption that would destroy the community that raised her; Vesper, seeing clearly at last, publicly renounces the inheritance. They end the festival together—café saved by community-backed funding, hearts no longer containable.
about_author: Paloma Kavanagh is a former line cook who writes love stories set in kitchens, festivals, and the fragile spaces between ambition and belonging. She lives in a coastal city where she still judges every romance by how it survives dessert.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Lie
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Facing foreclosure, she accepts Vesper's proposal: a fake relationship through his family's reunion weekend, catered by her café, paid enough to clear her debts. Their first staged date at a tasting feels dangerously unperformed by dessert. Emotional beat: guarded pragmatism cracking into reluctant curiosity as both pretend this is only business.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the family estate, Marguerite navigates hostile relatives while finding Vesper's hidden drafts—letters revealing his guilt over the development project gutting her neighborhood. A real almost-kiss after a power outage blurs every boundary they drew. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening as each realizes the other sees past their performance to the truth beneath.

chapters.title: What the Inheritance Costs
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She discovers the catering contract's fine print: her signature endorses the displacement of families she grew up with, including her aunt's bakery. Confronting Vesper, she learns he knew—and that his father weaponized her desperation. The festival opens amid rising tension; she must sign by midnight or lose everything. Emotional beat: betrayal, fury, and the terrible clarity of choosing between survival and integrity.

chapters.title: The Festival Ends
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, closing with both. At the gala, Vesper reads one unsent letter aloud, publicly renounces the inheritance, and exposes his father's scheme—torpedoing the contract and, briefly, them. But the community rallies: a cooperative fund saves Marguerite's café on its own terms. By the festival's last night, they choose each other freely, no lies left. Emotional beat: reckoning transformed into belonging, love chosen without transaction.
